display.title: Episode 238: The Dike (Tisha B'Av)
display.summary_short: Torah, prayer and kindness as a diet for the soul; the story of a girl lost when a dike broke and brought home years later by Shabbos candles; and the ancient melody of Eichah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast two days before Tisha B'Av 5746. Uncle Yossi explains that the world stands on three things, Torah, avodah (prayer) and acts of kindness, especially tzedakah, which refines the giver: the best diet for a healthy neshamah. A first-grade yeshiva boy with a very long name leads the Shema. Story time, 'The Dike': in a Dutch seaside town, two loving sisters, Leah and little Gittel, are in class when the dike bursts. Gittel, slowed by an old injury, falls asleep as the water rises and wakes in the cottage of a harsh old woman who tells her she has no family left. For three years she works from dawn to night and forgets that she is Jewish, until, walking home from a fair one Friday night, the glow of Shabbos candles in a window draws her in, and there she finds her own family. Uncle Yossi then speaks about music as Hashem's gift and introduces the one melody sung even on Tisha B'Av, the tune of Eichah. He ends with the customs of Tisha B'Av and asks children, too young to fast, to give tzedakah.
display.lesson: The Shabbos candles kept a lost Jewish child's heart alive and brought her home; Torah, prayer and kindness keep the soul strong.

date.note: 'Tomorrow is Erev Tisha B'Av' on a Tuesday (9 Av 5746 = Thu 1986-08-14). Most of the show also appears in episodes 136, 186, 389 and 488, so it may first have been recorded earlier.

advisories.note: A dike bursts and a town flees a flood; a child is nearly drowned.
A harsh woman keeps a lost Jewish girl for three years, tells her she has no family, works her hard and threatens beatings.
Tisha B'Av and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.

sources_cited.note: The world stands on three things: Torah, avodah and gemilus chasadim.
'Great is tzedakah, for it brings the Geulah closer.'
'Az yashir' read as 'will sing': the song of the future Geulah.

segments.title: Torah, Avodah and Kindness: A Diet for the Soul
segments.summary: The world stands on Torah, prayer and acts of kindness; tzedakah helps the poor and refines the giver.

segments.title: Shema with a first-grade yeshiva boy
The Dike
segments.summary: A little girl lost in a flood is raised by a harsh woman and forgets she is Jewish, until Shabbos candles in a window lead her back to her family.

segments.title: Music, Hashem's Gift, and the Song of Exile
segments.summary: Music lifts the soul; the Levi'im sang in the Beis HaMikdash and we will sing when Moshiach comes; even on Tisha B'Av there is the melody of Eichah.

segments.title: Tisha B'Av customs, and tzedakah for children
segments.summary: On Tisha B'Av the paroches is removed, we sit on the floor, wear no leather shoes, fast and read Eichah; children too young to fast give tzedakah.

relations.note: Episode 136 has the same talk, Shema guest and story; its opening differs. Possibly the original broadcast.
Episode 186 has the same talk, Shema guest and Dike story.
Episode 389 ('389 08-08-89') re-airs the same program, including the Erev Tisha B'Av ending.
Episode 488 re-airs the same talk, Shema guest and story.
'Torah Avoda Ge'mach 186' is the opening talk on Torah, avodah and kindness.
Same story, another telling: 'Gittel and the Candles: The Lost Sister' (Stories), told by unknown teller.
Same story, another telling: 'Gittel and the Shabbos Candles: A Chanukah Story' (Stories), told by Rabbi Chaim Levi Goldstein.

quality.notes: Largely a rebroadcast of an earlier Tisha B'Av program (see aired_again_in) with a current Erev Tisha B'Av ending. The Eichah chant is mostly untranscribed.

needs_human_review: Same program appears in episodes 136, 186, 389 and 488; decide which is the original and whether 238 is a rebroadcast.
